conclusion: No new logical unsoundness identified in the inspected subset-deletion adapter for valid generated single-query SMT input. This is not model qualification.
soundness_checks: Only whole top-level assert spans are deleted; no retained terms or definitions rewritten.
Final assert is retained byte-for-byte; exactly one check-sat, no assertion after it.
A fixed top-level command whitelist rejects echo, push/pop/reset and alternate check-sat commands.
Subset UNSAT accepted only with exit code zero and exact first stdout line unsat; subset SAT/unknown never accepted as original result.
Fallback runs unchanged original bytes and emits only an exact recognized first result line with exit code zero.
KEEP comment matching can change performance but every choice still yields a subset; correctness does not depend on semantic accuracy of comment labels.
Preparation verifies prior input SHA, creates distinct directory, copies independent theory/config, selects new adapter path and records new adapter/config hashes.

residual_risks.detail: Per-call files record argv, task bytes and solver stdout/stderr, but do not record subprocess exit codes, actual elapsed time, final selected branch/result or directly the solver binary hash. Parent model snapshot must continue to pin that binary; a future independent adapter version can persist complete call-result metadata.

The 5-second trial relies on Z3 -T rather than Python wall-clock subprocess timeout. Original fallback budget subtracts rounded elapsed time; startup/IO/kill overhead can exceed nominal outer wall budget. This is resource accounting, not a logical validity issue.

Parser validates command structure/whitelist, not full SMT sort/name correctness. The monotonicity claim assumes valid original single-query SMT generated by the locked Why3 pipeline. Unsupported/malformed cases must remain conservative errors/unknown in actual controls.
Static audit does not establish new byte/IEEE semantic model correctness, negative controls, solver stability or kernel acceptance.
